_comment: THE shared version-ordering corpus. Two independent comparators exist —
they had no corpus in common, so they could disagree about whether a peer
was older or newer and nothing would notice. Both consume this file; a case
added here is a case both must answer.
`expect` is the sign of compare(left, right): -1 left is older, 0 the same
release, 1 left is newer. Every case carries `why` because a version
ordering assertion with no stated reason cannot be reviewed.

cases.why: plain patch bump
this repo's 4-part X.Y.Z.N scheme: a build suffix is newer
missing trailing components are zero, not absent
a git tag's leading v is not part of the version
components compare numerically, never as strings

REGRESSION: a final release is newer than its own release candidate. The digit-scraping comparator read 0.5.0rc1 as [0,5,0,1] and called the candidate newer, so an operator running a prerelease was told to downgrade.
REGRESSION: 0.5.0rc1 and 0.5.0.1 both scraped to [0,5,0,1] and compared EQUAL, collapsing a prerelease and a real build into one version.
the pair the two regressions above have to stay consistent with
REGRESSION (PROGRAM.md §4): the semver punctuation spelling of the same defect
prereleases of one release order by their own number
alpha precedes beta regardless of the trailing number
beta precedes release candidate
dev builds precede every prerelease of the same release
a prerelease is still bounded by the next release
a prerelease of the next release is newer than the last release
prerelease labels are case-insensitive
scripts/ci.sh mints NETLLM_VERSION=<version>.ci for packaging smoke; an unrecognised trailing tag must not silently reorder anything
a peer that reports no version must not be ordered against, and must not raise
garbage from a peer is inert, not an exception — this comparator runs on data another machine on the LAN controls
long-form labels must rank like their short forms; the corpus only exercised a/b, so swapping alpha and beta in _PRERELEASE_RANK left the suite green
beta precedes rc, long form
dev precedes alpha, long form
pre is a prerelease and precedes the final release

preview, pre, c and rc are one tier -- PEP 440 normalises all four to rc, and this comparator agrees. Pinned because the corpus exercised only the short forms, so an accidental re-rank of the long ones stayed green
